profile.reading: Pearl Plaza Office Building sits at 601 East 18th Avenue in the North Capitol Hill neighborhood of Denver, Colorado, immediately east of the state capitol. Public address records identify the occupant of the building as the Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT), the state agency that runs shared computing and network infrastructure for Colorado state government. The building is a modest three story commercial office structure, not a purpose built or converted data center. It appears in this registry because an OpenStreetMap contributor tagged it with a CLLI code, a type of location identifier the telecommunications industry assigns to central offices and other facilities that carry telecom equipment, together with a general data center tag. That combination most plausibly reflects a telecom equipment room or network point of presence serving the tenants of the building and the state IT operations housed there, rather than a wholesale or retail colocation facility open to outside customers. No square footage, power capacity, or other data center specification is published for this address, because none applies to what public records indicate is a government office building rather than a dedicated data center.

reading.body:
This record cannot be read as a data center campus. The facility is registered at coordinates that reverse-geocode to a Colorado state government building, not a commercial data center operator. The operator field is blank because research identified no private operator to attribute to the name "Pearl Plaza Office Building," and registry policy prohibits guessing at an entity from a generic name alone.

The mismatch between the registered name and the address suggests either a data entry error in this registry or a misidentification of what occupies the location. Without a website, a confirmed operator, or published specifications for IT load, power capacity, or grid connection, this entry holds no information about AI infrastructure.

Colorado has 17 mapped facilities across the state, of which only 3 publish capacity figures totaling 26.35 MW. This record contributes neither a resolved operator nor a published megawatt figure to that state total. It remains an open research item pending manual review or a search tool capable of disambiguating the actual tenant or operator at this address.
